commits.summary: One Langfuse command for several sessions, and a session with nothing to send stops being reported
commits.body: sync.py check now gives one warning for all sessions whose end-of-turn hook did not finish a Langfuse send, with a single 'sync.py langfuse SID SID ...' command, instead of one warning and one command per session. sync.py langfuse already took several sessions; it now sends a session named twice once, and when it stops at a failure it prints the command for the sessions it had not reached.

commits.summary: Verification queue priorities: move committed jobs up or down later, and run only the top of the queue
commits.body: Job files are committed with the change they verify and not edited after, so a job's own priority was fixed at submit time and no job set one. verification/priorities.json now holds priorities by job id, each with a reason, set with 'pipeline.py prioritize ID... --priority N --reason TEXT' (--clear, no ids lists them). It overrides the job's own priority and is read at the same commit as the jobs. 'run --min-priority N' runs only the jobs at N or above and leaves the rest pending; 'status' lists pending jobs in start order with their priorities and says when priorities.json has uncommitted changes.

commits.summary: Record the user's decisions on the sound-verdicts brief's open items, and queue the job one of them waits on
commits.body:
Recorded under the brief's open questions (2026-11-06): the recorded examples' gap mode is decided once job 20261106-082917 is back (they stay in assume until then); a vacuous Verified keeps exit code 0; CI accepts proved and tested contracts for now, with the accepted evidence level to become configurable per project; the user reviews the benchmark's group 2 properties, the rest is accepted, and a CVE kernel is future work before any public claim; the landing page needs no update; the JBMC fork is decided from job -102624's ranking; the relative --jbmc path and the console report are fixed next, and fix-confined and --confirm with contracts get an analysis first.

Job 20261106-082917 is set to priority 10 in verification/priorities.json, so 'pipeline.py run --min-priority 10' now runs it with -073804 and -102624.

commits.summary: A relative --jbmc path is found, and --details prints the statement and the time under a verdict
commits.body:
A --jbmc path given relative to the current directory (bin/jbmc) passed the availability check, which runs where the command is started, then failed as 'JBMC produced no verdict: no output', since JBMC runs in the work directory. jbmc::executable makes such a path absolute where both drivers build their JBMC runs; a bare name is still looked up on PATH. Reproduced first with the previous binary on a one-line class, then fixed; unit test a_relative_jbmc_path_is_made_absolute_and_a_bare_name_is_left_to_path and CLI test a_relative_jbmc_path_is_found_from_the_current_directory on the real JBMC.

--details on prove and equivalence (lib/src/details.rs) prints, under the verdict, what --json holds as stated and search: the statement (domain, each assumption with its basis, what is observed, bounds, models, checker with solver and gap mode, confirmation, vacuity) and where the time went (the check's total, the driver's steps, and each checker run with its purpose, stage, ending, phase shares and formula size). The default report is unchanged. CLI test details_print_the_statement_and_where_the_time_went; lib/README.md documents both.

All Rust tests pass: 148 unit, 6 conformance, 62 integration. In the full run, on a loaded machine (635 s), the_tools_own_checker_agrees_with_jbmc_on_integer_proofs failed at its first assertion (the Pricing native regression proof, time-dependent, as recorded before); it passed alone in 16 s.
